text:
maria: Quick proposal — we need a standardized bench protocol to reliably compare kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV cache warmup, and quality tradeoffs (quant + speculative) across hardware. Current replay vs synthetic variance is making apples-to-apples impossible.

jon: +1. Can you sketch constraints? e.g., fixed seq lengths, deterministic seeds, warmup steps?

maria: Exactly. My draft: 1) deterministic traffic generator (seeded RNG) with per-user session traces, 2) canonical warmup: run N tokens with KV caching enabled to target 80% cache hit sim, 3) batching curve: sweep target_latency_ms -> max_batch, but keep same target_latency across HW, 4) quality checks: run eval set (perplexity / BLEU) after each quant/config, 5) regression gate rules (see below).

alex: How do you propose simulating multi-tenant interference? synthetic load rarely matches real tails.

maria: We'll have two modes: replay-harness (captures real traffic traces from prod; sanitized) and synthetic-protocol (parametric generator). The protocol specifies arrival distributions (Poisson + occasional bursts), correlation windows, and session lengths. Both modes use same warmup and batching config so results are comparable.

kevin: For KV cache behavior, we should capture prefix reuse distributions from our real traces and inject them into synthetic generator. Otherwise caching numbers won't match. I can export prefix histograms.

maria: Perfect. We'll include a 'prefix-reuse' profile file that the generator samples from. That will let us reproduce hit-rate curves.

jon: About regression gates — what metrics/thresholds? We need to balance perf and quality. My suggestion: p50 token latency should not regress >7% and p95 not >5% (relative) for the same throughput; quantization may be allowed if quality regression <=1.5% relative perplexity and human-eval drop <=2% on our small safety set. If either latency or quality crosses threshold, gate trips.

alex: I'm worried relative thresholds hide absolute degradations on high-throughput hardware. Maybe combine relative with absolute caps: p95 must remain <=200ms absolute for interactive models.

maria: Good call. New rule: require both relative and absolute checks. Add throughput-normalized unit-cost delta too (tokens/sec per GPU cost).

sara: How do we measure quality for speculative decoding experiments? Perplexity isn't always predictive of human-visible diffs.

maria: We'll run a small prompt suite (200 prompts) and compute: perplexity delta, exact-match for structured outputs, and a lightweight n-annotator human pass for a sample subset. For automated gating we use a composite quality score: 0.6*perplexity_norm + 0.4*task_acc_norm. If composite score crosses threshold, gate trips and we flag for manual review.

kevin: Do we have scripts? I can add a 'bench-proto' mode to the replay harness: ci/bench/harness.py --mode=protocol --profile=canonical --quant=8bit --speculative=on --target-latency=60

maria: Yes, let's standardize CLI. Also include an env var BENCH_SEED so runs are reproducible. Add --kv-profile <file>.

perf-bot: perf-bot: latest run 1771000000: model=gpt-medium variant=int8 speculative=off p95=142ms p50=22ms tok/s=120k kv_hit=73% cost/unit=$0.012

maria: Thanks perf-bot. We'll use that as a baseline for the first apples-to-apples sweep.

jon: Experiment plan: 1) baseline full-fp on hw-A and hw-B with replay traces, 2) synthetic-protocol sweep across target_latency [30,60,100]ms to map batching curves, 3) quant profiles: fp16, q4, q8, q8+speculative, 4) run eval suite after each step, 5) record kernel selection logs (runtime should dump kernel id per op) and capture perf counters.

alex: For kernel logs, add a compact csv output: op_name,kernel_id,seq_len,batch_size,latency_ms. Otherwise we won't be able to correlate kernel choice with hotspots.

maria: Agreed. Also record memory footprint and memcopy times. We want to detect cases where a faster kernel increases copy overhead and kills p95.

kevin: One more: KV cache warmup policy matters. We'll standardize on: run 150 tokens per session across 500 synthetic sessions before recording steady-state metrics. That approximates our 30-day median reuse.

sara: Who owns the regression gate? I'd prefer a lightweight automation: PRs that change runtime produce a bench run in CI; if gate trips, tests fail and require owner signoff. We already have deploy-bot integration for infra changes.

maria: I'll wire bench to CI. deploy-bot: can we fail CI on bench gate?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: yes — new pipeline job 'bench-gate' can return non-zero on gate trip and annotate PRs with the report. Need a service account with bench-run permissions.

jon: Timeline? We should run a first sweep this week on hw-A only just to validate tooling, then cross-hardware next week.

maria: I'll push the harness changes today and open a RFC doc with the protocol spec. Action items: @kevin export prefix histograms, @alex add kernel csv logging, @sara add composite quality scorer to eval harness. I'll post the RFC link when ready.

kevin: On it, will share histograms by EOD.

alex: I'll add csv logging and a small parser to the infra repo.

sara: I'll wire the composite scorer and add the 200-prompt suite.

maria: Thanks team — let's try to keep the initial sweep under 6 hours so CI can run a quick smoke. We'll iterate on thresholds after we get actual data. :rocket:
